title: Wikipedia (wikipedia.org)
description: Wikipedia is the free multilingual encyclopedia written and maintained by volunteers, hosting over 6 million English articles (tens of millions across 300+ languages). Its public content — articles, talk pages, revision histories — is freely readable and reusable under Creative Commons licensing. HONEST SCOPE NOTE: this directory is an expanding guide to major public sites; it does not and cannot list every website on earth.

print('wikipedia.org: free encyclopedia, 6M+ English articles, CC-licensed')
print('scope: an expanding directory of major public sites, not every site on earth')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Internet Archive (archive.org)
description: The Internet Archive is a nonprofit digital library offering free access to millions of books, films, software titles, and the Wayback Machine's archived web pages. Its public collections — including public-domain texts and the Open Library lending program — are among the web's most important public resources. Researchers use its archives to recover vanished pages and out-of-print works.
demo:
print('archive.org: Wayback Machine + millions of free books/films/software')
print('nonprofit digital library; public collections freely readable')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Project Gutenberg (gutenberg.org)
description: Project Gutenberg is the oldest digital library, founded by Michael Hart in 1971, offering over 70,000 free public-domain ebooks. Its public catalog spans classic literature, reference works, and historical documents, all freely downloadable in multiple formats. Volunteers proofread every text through Distributed Proofreaders.
demo:
print('gutenberg.org: 70,000+ free public-domain ebooks since 1971')
print('volunteer-proofread; multiple download formats')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Library of Congress (loc.gov)
description: The Library of Congress website publishes the nation's library online: millions of digitized photographs, maps, manuscripts, newspapers (Chronicling America), and the complete Congressional Record. Its public resources include copyright records, legislative information, and classroom materials. It is the largest library in the world, and its digital collections are free to all.
demo:
print('loc.gov: world\'s largest library online — photos, maps, newspapers, Congress records')
print('Chronicling America: free historic newspaper archive')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: NASA (nasa.gov)
description: NASA's public website publishes mission data, stunning image and video libraries, educational resources, and live coverage of launches and space station operations. Its public image archives — from Apollo to the James Webb Space Telescope — are freely usable with credit under NASA's media guidelines. The site also hosts open datasets and citizen-science projects.
demo:
print('nasa.gov: mission data, image/video libraries, open datasets')
print('Apollo to Webb imagery freely usable with credit')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: National Institutes of Health (nih.gov)
description: The NIH website is the public face of American medical research: PubMed's 35+ million biomedical citations, ClinicalTrials.gov's trial registry, MedlinePlus consumer health information, and open datasets from the Human Genome Project era onward. Its public resources are the first stop for evidence-based health information and research literature.
demo:
print('nih.gov: PubMed (35M+ citations), ClinicalTrials.gov, MedlinePlus')
print('public evidence-based health + research literature')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: National Weather Service (weather.gov)
description: The National Weather Service site provides free public forecasts, warnings, radar, and climate data for the entire United States, produced by NOAA. Its alert feeds (tornado, hurricane, flood warnings) save lives, and its APIs power countless weather apps. All of its data is public domain as U.S. government work.
demo:
print('weather.gov: free forecasts, warnings, radar, climate data (NOAA)')
print('public-domain data; powers countless weather apps')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: U.S. Census Bureau (census.gov)
description: The Census Bureau's public site publishes the decennial census, the American Community Survey, and economic censuses — the statistical portrait of the nation. Its data tools (data.census.gov) let anyone query population, housing, and business statistics down to the neighborhood level. Responses are confidential by law; only aggregated statistics are published.

print('census.gov: decennial census, American Community Survey, economic data')
print('individual responses confidential by law; aggregates public')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: BBC (bbc.com)
description: The BBC's public news site is one of the world's most-read news sources, funded in the UK by the licence fee and operating under a Royal Charter requiring impartiality. Its public output spans breaking news, analysis, documentaries, and the BBC World Service in dozens of languages. It is a primary global reference for international news.

print('bbc.com: global public news; charter-bound impartiality')
print('World Service in dozens of languages')
provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: World Health Organization (who.int)
description: The WHO website publishes global health data, disease outbreak information, technical guidelines, and the International Classification of Diseases. Its public dashboards tracked the COVID-19 pandemic worldwide, and its publications set norms for health systems everywhere. It is the UN's directing authority on international health.

print('who.int: global health data, outbreak info, ICD classifications')

provenance: Public reference: the sites' own published public pages; verified 2026-10-21.

title: UNESCO (unesco.org)
description: UNESCO's public site documents World Heritage Sites (1,100+ cultural and natural sites), education and science programs, and press-freedom initiatives. Its public lists — World Heritage, Memory of the World documentary heritage — are global reference standards for cultural preservation. The site publishes reports, statistics, and educational resources freely.

description: The World Bank's public site publishes development data, project documents, and research covering 189 member countries — including the open World Development Indicators database. Its public knowledge products on poverty, infrastructure, and climate finance guide policy worldwide. Project documents and procurement notices are published for transparency.

title: GitHub (github.com)
description: GitHub is the world's largest public code-hosting platform, home to hundreds of millions of repositories including vast open-source collections. Its public repositories — readable by anyone — are a working library of real software: libraries, tools, and complete applications. Developers learn by reading public code, and open-source collaboration happens in its pull requests and issues.

title: Stack Overflow (stackoverflow.com)
description: Stack Overflow is the public question-and-answer community where programmers have asked and answered tens of millions of coding questions since 2008. Its public archive — searchable, voted, and Creative Commons licensed — is the working reference desk of the software industry. The site's norms (specific questions, minimal reproducible examples) made it the template for expert Q&A.

print('stackoverflow.com: tens of millions of public coding Q&As since 2008')

title: White House (whitehouse.gov)
description: The White House website publishes the administration's public record: executive orders, proclamations, speeches, briefings, and policy fact sheets. Its archives preserve each administration's public output for the historical record. Researchers and citizens use it as the primary source for official executive-branch statements.
